steps.title: A blind tasting
steps.body: On 24 May 1976, British wine merchant Steven Spurrier organised a blind tasting in Paris. Nine French judges compared top Californian wines with top Bordeaux reds and Burgundy whites. Spurrier expected the French wines to win. A journalist from Time magazine, George Taber, was there.

steps.title: The results
steps.body: In the whites, Chateau Montelena's 1973 Chardonnay, from Napa, came first, ahead of Meursault and Puligny-Montrachet. In the reds, Stag's Leap Wine Cellars' 1973 Cabernet Sauvignon came first, ahead of Mouton Rothschild and Haut-Brion. Time reported it as the Judgment of Paris.

steps.prompt: Which Napa Cabernet won the red section in 1976?
steps.explanation: Chateau Montelena won the whites with Chardonnay.

steps.title: Impact
steps.body: The result shocked France and gave California, and the New World, credibility. Investment poured into Napa. A rematch in 2006, with the same wines aged 30 years, again placed Californian reds on top. The story became the film Bottle Shock in 2008. Bottles from the tasting are in the Smithsonian museum.

steps.prompt: What were the effects of the Judgment of Paris?
options: It banned French wine in the US

steps.title: What you learned
points: Steven Spurrier's 1976 blind tasting compared California and France
Chateau Montelena and Stag's Leap won
It gave the New World credibility
